title: Independent close and leadership
goal: Run a full close on your own, present a five-minute brief to Juan, and have the CPA or reviewer assess it.
concept_card: A controller runs the close on schedule, owns the controls even when busy, separates facts from estimates, sends policy questions to the CPA, and never lets an AI sign anything.
lesson_html:
Running the close yourself. Use your Module 4 checklist for every company. Keep a close calendar: bank feed daily, reconciliations by business day 5, intercompany by day 6, review by day 8, brief to Juan by day 10.

The five-minute brief.

  1. What changed from last month
  2. Why it changed, with the source
  3. What is uncertain or unknown
  4. Three decisions Juan needs to make

Separate facts (reconciled, sourced), estimates (with assumptions) and unknowns. Use plain language; skip the accounting terms.

Controls you own as controller

  • One person can't create a vendor, change its bank details and pay it
  • Journal entries above the limit need a second approval
  • Reopening a closed month needs approval
  • The approval matrix is written down and followed even when busy

Working with the CPA. Send the CPA tax questions, unusual transactions, accounting policy changes and anything going to a lender. Keep their answers in a policy register so you apply them the same way next time.
rule: AI makes you faster. It never signs anything and it is never the reviewer.

qbo_steps.title: Monthly close in each company
qbo_steps.html: Repeat the Module 4 steps in each QuickBooks company, one after another. Never combine companies in one file.

qbo_steps.title: Review what changed
qbo_steps.html: Reports → Profit and Loss Comparison (this month vs last month) to find what moved.

qbo_steps.title: Check user access
qbo_steps.html: ⚙ → Manage users. Confirm who can pay bills, edit vendors and change the closing date.

qbo_steps.title: Keep a management report
qbo_steps.html: Reports → Management reports lets you package the P&L, Balance Sheet and notes into one report for Juan.

scenario.text_html: For Juan's brief, reconciled cash on September 30: Twin Home Buyer $46,000, Matrix Group One $18,500, Peninsula Plumbing $9,200, Equity Track PH $3,300.
scenario.ask: What is total cash across the four companies?
scenario.explain: $46,000 + $18,500 + $9,200 + $3,300 = $77,000. Show each company on its own line too, and note that this total is not all available to spend.
scenario.followup: The AI’s summary says all accounts reconciled. What do you check before believing it?

quiz.q: You want to include a number in Juan's brief but can't find its source. You…
options: Write "unknown" and say what's needed to get it
Ask the AI for a number
quiz.why: An unsourced number is worse than an honest "unknown."
quiz.followup: Juan asks you to show a lender “about $250,000 of equity.” What do you need before you say a number?

quiz.q: The AI says an account is reconciled. Is it?
options: Only after you check it against the statement and a reviewer signs off
Yes, if two AI tools agree
Yes, if the difference is under $100
quiz.why: AI can help find matches. Evidence and human sign-off decide.

quiz.q: Juan says to skip the reviewer this month because everyone is busy. You…
options: Explain the risk, and either get a lighter review or document that he approved the exception
Ask the AI to review instead
quiz.why: Controls matter most when busy. If skipped, it's a documented, approved exception.

quiz.q: A lender asks for a signed financial statement. Who handles it?
options: You prepare; the CPA or authorized person reviews and signs
quiz.why: Lender reporting needs qualified review and a named signer.

options: Three consecutive clean closes with reviewer-approved balances and clear briefs
quiz.why: The title follows consistent, demonstrated performance.

task: Run the full month-end close for every company on your own. Present the five-minute brief to Juan. The CPA or reviewer assesses the close and the brief.
rubric: Every material balance supported and reviewer-approved
Brief separates facts, estimates and unknowns
